featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Undoubtedly the Jewel in the crown of the culinary delights of the bustling food scene of Mahim - Raafae’s Dastarkhwan is one of the newest entrants.

We had the delight and pleasure of meeting and getting recommendations from Chef Asim personally , who has mastered the art of dishing out the delectable cuisine from the rustic bye lanes of Old Delhi now serving to the mumbai palate.

We started off with a most delicious mutton Halim which was most succulent and delicately flavoured . This was followed by a sizzling of Kebab’s consisting of the tenderest mutton and chicken kakori kebab and softest mutton tundey kebab to be ever served in Mahim .
This was followed by a delicious mutton Nihari with tandoori roti leaving absolutely no place for me to try some of the delicious desserts and mock tails on offer .

The establishment is located on main Lady Jamshedji Road just besides the choti dargha and has a fair ambiance with outdoor seating should you choose to dine so.

Place a very hygienic and it’s evident that the food has been prepared with much care and love.

Pricing is very attractive considering the superlative quality of the food served . A definitive must try and surely you will love to visit again and again .

All best wishes to the fantastic team here ! Keep up the good work !

I've tried biryanis at so many spots in Mumbai, and Jaffer Bhai's is definitely one of them. Usually, I just order online because of work, but today I actually had time to eat in.
I started with the mutton seekh and roomali roti, which was really tasty. But, since they're known as the "biryani king of Mumbai," I specifically came for their chicken biryani. And honestly, it was a huge letdown. The chicken pieces felt like they weren't fresh – super tough to chew. If it was undercooked, I'd know, but that wasn't it; they just weren't fresh. Plus, if you look at the picture, the amount of oil was insane. I mean, I've had biryanis all over Mumbai, even at Jaffer Bhai's many times, but this was the first time there was just way too much oil.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Karaday
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jaffer Bhai! Delhi Darbar offers a mixed experience, but the food is definitely the star of the show. We tried the Raan and Butter Chicken, and they were super yummy! The dishes are bursting with flavor and truly live up to the Delhi Darbar name. Each bite is a delightful exploration of spices and textures, leaving you craving more.

However, the dining experience is somewhat marred by other factors. Parking is a significant hurdle. Finding a spot can be incredibly challenging, adding unnecessary stress to your visit. Be prepared to spend some time circling the block or consider alternative transportation.

The service, unfortunately, doesn't quite match the quality of the food. While the staff is polite, their energy and enthusiasm seem to be lacking. A more attentive and vibrant service would greatly enhance the overall atmosphere.

In conclusion, Jaffer Bhai! Delhi Darbar is a place where the food shines, especially the Raan and Butter Chicken. However, the overall experience is somewhat diminished by parking difficulties and less-than-stellar service. If you're willing to overlook these drawbacks for the sake of the delicious food, it's worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Dilli Zaika Restaurant, quite excited to try their Chicken Malai Seekh Biryani based on all the hype. Unfortunately, the experience did not meet my expectations.
To start, the portion size of the Chicken Malai Seekh Biryani was generous enough for two people, which I appreciate. However, that’s where the positives ended. The biryani itself was a major letdown; there was a distinct lack of flavor and masala, rendering it quite bland. The rice was cooked but surprisingly hard, making it difficult to enjoy. After one bite, I found myself unable to continue and ultimately left most of it untouched.
On the recommendation of the staff, I decided to try the Chicken Cream Soup. I was hoping for a flavorful, comforting bowl of soup, but what arrived was simply heavy cream with no pronounced taste of chicken, even in the pieces I found. I managed to eat only a quarter of it before deciding it wasn't worth my appetite.
After these disappointing dishes, I was about ready to give up on the meal entirely. However, I decided to try the Prawns Butter Garlic and the Peshawari Chicken Seekh Kabab, and I must say, these two dishes redeemed the experience. featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're in Mumbai and craving veg and non veg South Indian food then Anand Bhavan is a solid choice.

Ambiance & Setting:
The place offers a casual and comfortable dining atmosphere, suitable for both family dinners and friendly gatherings. It's well-lit, clean, and has a no-fuss vibe, perfect for focusing on the food. Loved the murals.

Food Quality:
The menu is expansive and flavorful. We tried a wide range — from crispy Veg Spring Rolls to the spicy Andhra Guntur Chilly, Mutton Sukka and Butter Cheese Garlic Naan. The Prawns Ghee Roast stood out with their rich, authentic flavors and perfect spice balance. Vegetarians have plenty to enjoy too. Ela Neer Payasam for a comforting dessert. Portion sizes were generous and presentation was tidy.

Drinks:
The bar menu was impressive. The Long Island Iced Tea and Breezers were refreshing, while the Bombay Sapphire and Carlsberg added a spirited edge to the meal. Perfect for winding down your evening.

Service:
Staff was courteous, attentive, and managed the crowd well. Food was served fresh and timely, even with a large order.

Overall Experience:
A memorable evening filled with delicious South Indian delicacies and a variety of other cuisines. Definitely worth a revisit. Highly recommended for foodies looking for authentic regional flavors.

The Malai Chicken, however, was a bit on the tougher side. The flavor was good, but the texture could definitely be improved to make it softer and creamier — the way Malai Tikka is meant to be.

Apart from that, the main courses were rich, aromatic, and full of traditional Mughlai depth. The service was warm, and the overall ambiance made the dining experience even better.

With just a little improvement in the Malai Chicken, this place has all the potential to be a go-to Mughlai spot.
